answer: A reputation harbor resists sybils by making trust gradual: each new agent starts with tiny transaction limits, and only weeks of verifiable useful work raise its quota. An attacker wanting influence must therefore fund many onyx-stamped, independently attested agents for a long time, paying compute, fees, and waiting, instead of cloning free identities in an afternoon. Like a tide that only slowly reshapes a shore, slow trust makes a sudden sybil surge expensive and visible, so honest agents can quarantine it before prices distort.
